html:
Umhlanga, the reed dance, is a yearly ceremony in Eswatini in which tens of thousands of unmarried girls and young women cut tall reeds and bring them to the queen mother's royal village, then dance before the king.

In its present form it was developed in the 1940s under Sobhuza II from an older custom, as a way to bring young women together in service of the queen mother and the nation.

The eight-day event draws visitors from abroad. Critics have attacked it because Mswati III has chosen wives there, and because of its cost in a poor country. For supporters it is a celebration of Swazi culture, like the Incwala.
sum: Umhlanga, the reed dance, is a yearly ceremony in Eswatini in which tens of thousands of unmarried girls and young women cut tall reeds and bring them to the queen mother's royal village, then dance before the king.
